posts.title: i did not take my own advice!
posts.description: who ever does really? i dusted this thing off because i was starting to get that feeling im sure you're familiar with, that you're wasting your precious time on this earth. i stand by everything on my home page, even now, but the scariest thing is that you can know that you're not spending your time doing what you really want to.. and you just can't stop being stuck in the cycle of NOT doing it. backrooms is one of my favourite movies of the year because it got that point across to me in a way that got under my skin. im stunned by an inability to break cycles that only harm me. i think im quite a vulnerable person. i struggle with a lot of really severe mental illness, and i think that compromises my ability to do a lot of things effectively. the best comparison i can make is that i feel like agni from fire punch most of the time. my mind is always on fire. it can get pretty difficult to tell what parts are just mental illness and what parts are my soul burning in defiance to the life

posts.title: i played resistance 3
posts.description: it sucked. sort of. the ending definitely did. i feel like i was somewhat oversold on how good it was going to be compared to the other two games, definitely on the narrative side of things. "it has a great story, the protagonist is so much better than nathan hale". it feels to me that a lot of gamers have very little exposure to genuinely good writing. the only difference between nathan and joseph is.. joseph has a reason for involving himself in the chimerian war... thing is... a motivation for your characters... is bare minimum. he doesn't talk during gameplay, and characters rarely speak to him beyond bland, almost pointless exposition. i am willing to forgive nathan being mute, i have less forgiveness for joseph. 2006 and 2011 are worlds apart, and a totally mute (during gameplay) protagonist in a story-driven game released during 2011 feels a bit antiquated, even if it still wasn't entirely the norm in fps games. then again... insomniac have never been ones for innovation really,
